# S·P·A Diagnostic Playbook {#sec-appendix-spa}

When the base of the warehouse mobile manipulator stops past its rack-end clearance, the cause could be stale sensor evidence (Sense), an infeasible waypoint (Plan), or a worn brake that delivers less deceleration than assumed (Act). The **S·P·A taxonomy** locates the first broken contract among **Sense**, **Plan**, and **Act**. Logs and physical measurements then test that diagnosis before a remedy is admitted.

## How to Use This Appendix {.unnumbered}

Use this diagnostic playbook when an embodied system violates a safety envelope, misses an execution deadline, chatters during contact, or trips hardware interlocks. Work through the diagnosis in four systematic passes:

1. **State the physical symptom and binding budget**: Record the observed stopping-distance breach, contact-force transient, thermal trip, or enforcer deadline overrun, including units, load, operating state, and the limit configured for that machine.
2. **Localize the candidate axis or intersection**: Use @tbl-spa-components-ref for a first pass across the three core axes. When the symptom involves interface timing, state representations, or actuation authority, move directly to the intersection landscape in @tbl-spa-intersections.
3. **Test the quantitative hypothesis**: Measure the candidate constraint or budget using the instruments in @tbl-spa-troubleshooting, such as timestamp skew, bus queue time, phase current, or tracking error.
4. **Intervene and remeasure across the causal boundary**: Apply a remedy and rerun the measured test over the declared load, timing, and fault envelope.

The physical symptom determines the most effective entry point. Unstable contact oscillations should immediately examine the Act–Sense ($A \cap S$) boundary. A sudden reference discontinuity or measured torque transient points to the Plan–Act ($P \cap A$) boundary. Phantom obstacle braking or drift under occlusion points to the Sense–Plan ($S \cap P$) interface. Deadline jitter during concurrent neural inference points directly to the permission decision at the center ($S \cap P \cap A$).

## Diagnostic Summary of the S·P·A Axes {#sec-appendix-spa-summary}

The S·P·A taxonomy decomposes the cyber-physical loop into three axes. @Tbl-spa-components-ref lists a constraint or budget to inspect for each one; these are not all conservation laws.

\Needspace{28\baselineskip}

| Axis          | Operational role                    | Constraint or budget to test                                                     | Diagnostic action                                                                              | Book locus                                |
|:--------------|:------------------------------------|:---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|
| **Sense (S)** | Capture and estimate physical state | Evidence age, field of view, clock conversion, uncertainty, and sensor transport | Compare capture and per-cell evidence epochs with a measured state and the permission deadline | @sec-perception, @sec-memory              |
| **Plan (P)**  | Propose a target and trajectory     | Intent validity, compute latency, dynamics, and stopping-suffix admission        | Compare proposed targets and future states with independently checked limits                   | @sec-training, @sec-intent, @sec-planning |
| **Act (A)**   | Apply and measure force             | Current, torque, thermal headroom, brake response, and kinetic clearance         | Measure command-to-force response and achieved stop under the declared load                    | @sec-body, @sec-nervous, @sec-enforcement |

: **S·P·A axis reference**: The axes organize diagnosis around measured constraints and budgets, with the chapter that develops each contract. {#tbl-spa-components-ref tbl-colwidths="[12,18,30,27,13]"}

While this single-axis separation is helpful for initial triage, production failures rarely originate within a single isolated component. More frequently, the failure sits at the **boundary** between two axes—such as an unblended trajectory step that excites high mechanical rotor inertia, or camera direct memory access (DMA) ingress that saturates the memory crossbar needed by real-time motor timers. Resolving these failures requires mapping the intersection landscape.

## The Intersection Landscape {#sec-appendix-spa-intersections}

@Fig-spa-triad shows how Sense, Plan, and Act intersect, with the permission decision at the center where all three meet. In this appendix, we formalize this landscape into an operational systems diagnostic matrix.

::: {#fig-spa-triad fig-env="figure" fig-pos="t" fig-cap="**The S·P·A intersection landscape**: Sense, Plan, and Act meet pairwise in three physical decisions, locating the object now, checking that proposed motion fits limits, and measuring what changed after acting. Their center is the permission decision, where an independent permission path checks the shared physical budget before actuation." fig-alt="Three overlapping circles labeled Sense, Plan, and Act. Sense and Plan ask where an object is now. Plan and Act ask whether motion fits physical limits. Act and Sense ask what changed. The center, where all three overlap, is the independent permission decision."}
![](../01_boundary/images/svg/fig01_spa_triad.svg){width="95%"}
:::

Each intersection is a testable handoff. @Tbl-spa-intersections names the failure mode and the evidence needed before a proposed fix earns permission.

| Intersection                     | Handoff contract                                           | Failure to test                                                                | Evidence and candidate remedy                                                                                            |
|:---------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$S\cap P$** — belief           | Observations become timed, framed state estimates          | A fresh map publication hides an old voxel or an unseen object remains unknown | Check per-cell evidence epochs, free vs. occupied rays, and frame transforms; use a separately validated collision layer |
| **$P\cap A$** — motion           | A proposal becomes an admitted, state-matched trajectory   | A seam requests a torque transient or the stop suffix no longer fits clearance | Check entry state, derivatives, lease, and clearance; reject an infeasible seam and use the resident stop                |
| **$A\cap S$** — feedback         | Actuation changes the state that sensors report            | Contact force rises before the next useful sample or an actuator saturates     | Measure command-to-force and sensor-return delay; choose a local reflex and passive limit where justified                |
| **$S\cap P\cap A$** — permission | The independent gate turns a proposal into physical action | Compute, memory, power, or clock interference delays refusal                   | Measure response under contention; revoke tracking and qualify isolation or relocate the path if its bound fails         |

: **The S·P·A intersection taxonomy**: Four handoffs locate the earliest broken physical contract and the evidence required to repair it; the axis reference above links to the underlying chapters. {#tbl-spa-intersections tbl-colwidths="[16,23,27,34]"}

### $S \cap P$ spatial belief and epistemic handoffs {#sec-appendix-spa-belief}

The Sense--Plan ($S \cap P$) intersection formalizes the **epistemic handoff**: translating raw, asynchronous, multi-modal sensor observations into a metric, temporally certified spatial belief state that planning algorithms and affordance models can query without executing ungrounded actions. This handoff bridges Part II and Part III of the book, taking sensor calibration and domain bounds from the Provenance Record (@sec-data) and observation streams from the Perception Evidence contract (@sec-perception) to populate the Scene Memory State (@sec-memory).

In an embodied machine, the primary handoff contract requires that every spatial cell or bounding volume in the occupancy representation $\mathcal{M}$ carries an explicit evidence epoch $t_\text{evidence}$ and a tri-state classification: observed free ($\mathcal{M}_\text{free}$), observed occupied ($\mathcal{M}_\text{occ}$), or unobserved unknown ($\mathcal{M}_\text{unknown}$). The permission path enforces a strict epistemic invariant before any trajectory planner may claim clearance through a spatial volume:
$$\tau_\text{age} = t_\text{curr} - t_\text{evidence} + \tau_\text{sync\_error} \le \tau_\text{valid}$$
where $\tau_\text{sync\_error}$ is the bounded Precision Time Protocol (PTP) synchronization uncertainty across sensor clocks (@sec-appendix-systems-timers). If $\tau_\text{age} > \tau_\text{valid}$, the cell's status degrades from certified free space to uncertified unknown space.

Crucially, **unknown space is hazardous until cleared by active sightlines**. Planning algorithms must never equate unobserved space with traversable free space. When an obstacle passes behind an occluding pallet or wall, the absence of an active sensor return represents a lack of information, not free volume. The failure to maintain this invariant produces three characteristic failure modes:

1. *Epistemic blindness*: The planner plans aggressive trajectories through unobserved space, treating unmapped blind spots as empty. If an obstacle or human steps from behind a blind corner, the machine cannot stop within its remaining sensing margin.
2. *Phantom obstacles and stale log-odds*: When dynamic obstacles vacate a region, failure to project negative evidence along sensor optical rays leaves positive log-odds in the Truncated Signed Distance Field (TSDF) or voxel memory (@sec-appendix-ml-voxels). The machine initiates uncommanded emergency stops in visibly clear aisles.
3. *Extrinsic calibration drift and spatial skew*: Mechanical vibration or thermal warping alters the coordinate frame transform $^{B}\mathbf{T}_C$ between sensors and the mobile base. 3D bounding boxes warp into ground planes, corrupting affordance pre-conditions (@sec-intent) and causing grasping or navigation failures.

Diagnostic testing for $S \cap P$ failures begins by inspecting raw sensor-to-map latency, comparing the per-voxel evidence epoch against ground-truth measurements, and validating raycast eviction queues.

### $P \cap A$ admitted motion and kinetic seam feasibility {#sec-appendix-spa-motion}

The Plan--Act ($P \cap A$) intersection governs the **kinetic handoff**: admitting candidate trajectory setpoints proposed by statistical neural policies (Brain) and converting them into continuous, dynamically feasible joint commands executed by motor drives (Body). This interface bridges the Intent Specification (@sec-intent), Policy Manifest (@sec-training), and Trajectory Plan (@sec-planning) against the physical plant ceilings recorded in the Limit Record (@sec-body).

Modern generative policies---such as diffusion decoders and vision-language-action (VLA) models---propose actions in discrete horizons or chunks ($K$ waypoints spanning duration $K \Delta t$). The permission path cannot admit a raw chunk as an open-loop actuator reference. Instead, the seam connecting the currently executing trajectory to the incoming proposal must satisfy $C^2$ continuity with the measured plant state:
$$\mathbf{q}(t_0^+) = \mathbf{q}(t_0^-), \quad \dot{\mathbf{q}}(t_0^+) = \dot{\mathbf{q}}(t_0^-), \quad \ddot{\mathbf{q}}(t_0^+) = \ddot{\mathbf{q}}(t_0^-)$$
where $t_0$ is the handover epoch, and continuity is enforced by quintic polynomial blending (@sec-appendix-control-splines). Furthermore, the entire admitted trajectory chunk must satisfy joint velocity limits $\lVert \dot{\mathbf{q}} \rVert \le \dot{\mathbf{q}}_{\max}$, acceleration limits $\lVert \ddot{\mathbf{q}} \rVert \le \ddot{\mathbf{q}}_{\max}$, and jerk ceilings $\lVert \dddot{\mathbf{q}} \rVert \le \mathbf{j}_{\max}$.

The fundamental safety guarantee of the $P \cap A$ boundary is the **reserved stopping suffix** (@sec-planning). The permission path admits a chunk if and only if, at every point along the chunk horizon, there exists an executable deceleration profile that can bring the machine to a complete stop inside the currently validated clear distance $d_\text{clear}(t)$:
$$d_\text{stop}(v) = \frac{v^2}{2 a_\text{brake}} + v \tau_\text{delay} \le d_\text{clear}(t)$$
where $a_\text{brake}$ is the verified constant deceleration equivalent to the $C^2$ stopping spline (@sec-enforcement) and $\tau_\text{delay}$ accounts for sensor age, enforcer cycle time, and brake response latency.

Violating $P \cap A$ contracts leads to severe physical damage:

1. *Seam torque shock*: Concatenating consecutive chunks without $C^2$ acceleration matching commands a step change in acceleration ($\Delta \ddot{\mathbf{q}} \ne 0$). High-ratio gearboxes magnify this discontinuity through reflected rotor inertia:
   $$\tau_\text{motor} = N^2 J_\text{rotor} \ddot{\theta} + \tau_\text{load}$$
   producing multi-kiloampere phase current spikes ($I_\text{peak} > 3 I_\text{rated}$) within sub-millisecond intervals. These spikes shear planetary gearbox gear teeth, break drive shafts, or trip inverter overcurrent protections.
2. *Terminal trapping and stopping-suffix exhaustion*: The policy plans an aggressive motion into a narrow corridor without reserving sufficient braking distance. When an obstacle emerges, the machine is kinodynamically committed; even full emergency braking breaches the safety perimeter.
3. *Inference tail underflow*: Generative diffusion inference exhibits heavy tail latencies ($Q_{1-\epsilon}(L_\text{inf}) > K \Delta t$). When an inference burst exceeds the buffer duration, the executor starves, forcing an abrupt transfer to fallback braking.

Diagnostic action requires measuring oscilloscope current traces at chunk boundaries, checking lease expiration timers against measured inference tails, and confirming that every admitted plan reserves its stopping suffix.

### $A \cap S$ physical feedback, contact dynamics, and reflex latency {#sec-appendix-spa-feedback}

The Act--Sense ($A \cap S$) intersection closes the causal loop across the **causal boundary**: actuator forces move joints and exert contact forces against the environment, altering physical reality, which is then captured by sensors and fed back into the control loop. Governed by the Limit Record (@sec-body), Transport Budget (@sec-nervous), and Evaluation Summary (@sec-evaluation), this boundary embodies the First Law of Physical AI: irreversibility. Energy delivered into a physical contact cannot be recalled.

The cyber-physical contract governing $A \cap S$ is **passivity and phase margin under contact stiffness**. When an end-effector or wheel contacts a rigid environment characterized by stiffness $k_\text{env}$, the closed-loop system is stable only if the total sensor-to-actuator transport latency $\tau_\text{loop}$ satisfies the critical stability threshold:
$$\tau_\text{loop} < \tau_\text{crit} \approx \sqrt{\frac{M}{k_\text{env}}}$$
where $M$ is the effective reflected mass at the contact interface. When interacting with stiff objects (such as steel latches, concrete uprights, or rigid bins where $k_\text{env} > 10^5\text{ N/m}$), $\tau_\text{crit}$ drops below $5\text{ ms}$. If feedback is routed through a remote neural planner running at $20\text{ Hz}$ ($\tau = 50\text{ ms}$), the loop delay introduces excess phase lag ($\phi_\text{lag} = \omega \tau_\text{loop}$) exceeding $180^\circ$, transforming negative feedback into destabilizing positive feedback.

Failure modes at the $A \cap S$ boundary present clear physical signatures:

1. *Contact hunting and limit-cycle chatter*: During assembly or door-opening tasks, the manipulator chatters against the latch or frame, oscillating violently between maximum commanded torque and zero contact. This chatter induces high-frequency fatigue, chips tooling, and overheats motor windings.
2. *Impact force blowup*: A high-speed position reference commands motion past a rigid surface. Before perception or remote force telemetry detects the contact, force rises linearly with penetration ($F = k_\text{env} \Delta x$), easily exceeding structural yield limits ($F > F_\text{yield}$) and permanently bending robot linkages.
3. *Closed-loop covariate drift*: In open-loop simulation or offline dataset evaluation, policy error may appear negligible. When deployed in closed-loop physical environments, small heading biases ($\epsilon_\theta$) integrate through unicycle kinematics ($y(t) \approx \int v \sin \epsilon_\theta \, dt$), causing compounding error ($\mathcal{O}(T^2 \epsilon)$, @sec-appendix-ml-compounding) that veers the machine into warehouse racks.

To guarantee stability at the $A \cap S$ boundary, high-stiffness contact must never rely on high-latency neural inference. Instead, the architecture must delegate contact regulation to local, hardware-level impedance or admittance loops executing on dedicated motor microcontrollers at $1\text{ kHz}$, backed by passive mechanical compliance (such as series-elastic elements or rubber dampers, @sec-body).

### $S \cap P \cap A$ independent permission decisions and silicon isolation {#sec-appendix-spa-permission}

At the center of the triad sits the tripartite intersection where Sense, Plan, and Act converge: the **independent permission decision**. This is the physical realization of the Third Law of Physical AI: **proposal is not permission**. The statistical Brain proposes candidate trajectories; the Nervous System arbitrates permission against hard physical invariants; the Body actuates only what is admitted.

The permission path executes on an isolated, deterministic compute enclave (a dual-core lockstep safety microcontroller or hard real-time RTOS core) with hard worst-case execution time (WCET) bounds. In every cycle ($200\text{ Hz}\text{--}1\text{ kHz}$), the enforcer evaluates candidate setpoints against a formal safety filter, such as a Control Barrier Function Quadratic Program (CBF-QP, @sec-enforcement, @sec-appendix-control-cbf):
$$\min_{\mathbf{u}} \frac{1}{2} \lVert \mathbf{u} - \mathbf{u}_\text{prop} \rVert^2 \quad \text{s.t.} \quad \nabla h(\mathbf{x}) \cdot f(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{u}) + \alpha(h(\mathbf{x})) \ge 0, \quad \mathbf{u} \in \mathcal{U}_\text{admissible}$$
where $h(\mathbf{x}) \ge 0$ defines the forward-invariant safe set $\mathcal{C}$ (including obstacle clearance buffers, kinematic joint envelopes, and thermal limits), and $\mathbf{u}_\text{prop}$ is the candidate setpoint proposed by the Brain. If the QP is feasible, the optimal filtered command $\mathbf{u}^*$ is dispatched to the motor drives. If the QP fails, times out, or encounters missing sensor evidence, the enforcer revokes the execution token and autonomously executes the resident state-matched stop without querying the Brain.

The primary challenge at the $S \cap P \cap A$ intersection is **silicon and electrical interference** between the uncertified statistical Brain and the certified deterministic enforcer (@sec-placement):

1. *Memory crossbar and DRAM contention*: When high-resolution camera streams transfer frames via DMA across shared System-on-Chip (SoC) AXI crossbars, memory controller queues saturate. If the real-time enforcer core shares this DRAM or bus, memory fetch latencies spike, causing the enforcer thread to miss its hard $1\text{ ms}$ real-time deadline.
2. *Inductive power rail droop ($L \, dI/dt$)*: Heavy neural network inference bursts on NPUs or GPUs cause sudden current transients ($dI/dt > 100\text{ A}/\mu\text{s}$). Parasitic inductances in shared power distribution networks induce voltage droop ($\Delta V = L \, dI/dt$), depressing supply rails below microcontroller brownout thresholds and triggering spontaneous watchdog resets.
3. *Premise violation and epistemic invalidation*: The CBF mathematical guarantee holds only if its physical premises hold. If the enforcer assumes a dry concrete floor ($\mu \ge 0.7$) but an uninspected oil spill reduces friction to $\mu \le 0.15$ (@sec-frontier), the solver computes an optimal command that physical tire contact forces cannot realize, leading to boundary penetration despite a provably optimal solver status.

Resolving $S \cap P \cap A$ failures requires physical hardware isolation: pinning the enforcer to tightly coupled memory (TCM) on dedicated microcontroller silicon, enforcing AXI Quality-of-Service (QoS) bus arbitration, isolating electrical power rails with independent buck regulators, and maintaining an explicit register of uncertified physical premises (@sec-frontier).

## Architectural Contract Lineage Across Chapters 01 to 17 {#sec-appendix-spa-lineage}

The seventeen chapters of this book form an unbroken chain of cyber-physical custody, formalizing the transition from statistical machine learning to certified physical work. Every chapter from @sec-body to @sec-frontier either produces or qualifies a concrete, typed contract record defined in `mlsysim` (@sec-boundary-book-architecture). @Tbl-spa-lineage maps this sixteen-record lineage across the four governing laws, locating each contract on its primary S·P·A axis or intersection.

| Chapter and title                           | Contract record                                     | S·P·A locus       | Physical invariant enforced                                                                                                       | Primary failure mode diagnosed                                                                            |
|:--------------------------------------------|:----------------------------------------------------|:------------------|:----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| @sec-body: The Physical Body                | Limit Record (`LimitRecord`)                        | Act, $A \cap S$   | Motor torque $\tau \le \tau_{\max}$, thermal dissipation $I_\text{rms} \le I_\text{cont}$, stopping distance $d_\text{stop}(v)$   | Inverter thermal trip, rotor resonance, structural yield                                                  |
| @sec-brain: The Cognitive Brain             | Proposal Record (`ProposalRecord`)                  | Plan              | Chunk horizon $K$, candidate setpoint bounds, proposer lease request                                                              | Unbounded candidate setpoints, unconstrained sampling cadence                                             |
| @sec-nervous: The Nervous System            | Transport Budget (`TransportBudget`)                | $S \cap P \cap A$ | Bus cycle time $T_\text{bus}$, jitter bound $\sigma_t \le \sigma_{\max}$, proposal lease ceiling $\tau_\text{lease}$              | Fieldbus priority inversion, seqlock torn read, lease expiration overrun                                  |
| @sec-data: Physical Data                    | Provenance Record (`ProvenanceRecord`)              | Sense, $S \cap P$ | Dataset calibration bounds, ODD operational envelope limits                                                                       | Covariate shift, out-of-distribution actuation commands                                                   |
| @sec-training: Policy Training              | Policy Manifest (`PolicyManifest`)                  | Plan              | Denoising step count $N_\text{step}$, chunk horizon $K$, Lipschitz constant $L_\pi$                                               | Multimodal mode-averaging collapse, explosive policy Lipschitz constant                                   |
| @sec-evaluation: Closed-Loop Evaluation     | Evaluation Summary (`EvaluationSummary`)            | $A \cap S$        | Closed-loop rollout stability, $\mathcal{O}(T^2 \epsilon)$ compounding drift bounds, collision rate $\lambda_\text{collision}$    | Open-loop loss deception, unmodeled closed-loop yaw drift                                                 |
| @sec-perception: Sensor Perception          | Perception Evidence (`PerceptionEvidence`)          | Sense             | Observation age $\tau_\text{obs}$, PTP timestamp sync error $\tau_\text{sync} \le 1.0\,\mu\text{s}$, bounding covariance $\Sigma$ | Rolling shutter distortion, timestamp skew, camera extrinsic calibration drift                            |
| @sec-memory: Spatial Memory                 | Scene Memory State (`SceneMemoryState`)             | $S \cap P$        | Per-cell evidence epoch $t_\text{evidence}$, tri-state classification (free/occupied/unknown), raycasting eviction                | Phantom obstacle emergency stops, stale voxel retention, unobserved space mistaken for free space         |
| @sec-intent: Grounded Intent                | Intent Specification (`IntentSpecification`)        | Plan              | Task tolerance bounds $r_{x,y,z}$, affordance predicate validity, terminal mode admissibility                                     | Affordance hallucination, ungrounded task goal selection                                                  |
| @sec-planning: Trajectory Planning          | Trajectory Plan (`TrajectoryPlan`)                  | $P \cap A$        | $C^2$ quintic polynomial seam continuity, joint jerk ceilings $\mathbf{j} \le \mathbf{j}_{\max}$, stopping suffix guarantee       | Seam velocity/acceleration discontinuity, reflected rotor inertia shock, stop suffix exhaustion           |
| @sec-enforcement: Safety Enforcement        | Admitted Command (`AdmittedCommand`)                | $S \cap P \cap A$ | Forward invariance via CBF-QP filtering, WCET $\le 1.0\text{ ms}$, resident state-matched stop ownership                          | Infeasible QP projection, enforcer deadline overrun, unsafe command leakage to motor registers            |
| @sec-placement: Workload Placement          | Deployment Envelope (`DeploymentEnvelope`)          | $S \cap P \cap A$ | Silicon partitioning, dedicated TCM memory, AXI QoS priorities, inductive voltage droop $\Delta V < 5\%$                          | Shared memory bus contention, DRAM bank conflict, power rail brownout during NPU bursts                   |
| @sec-intervention: Supervisory Intervention | Intervention Event (`InterventionEvent`)            | $S \cap P \cap A$ | Four-phase bumpless transfer, supervisory token state machine, contact-force relaxation                                           | Intervention takeover jerk, operator authority lock-out, transfer state discontinuity                     |
| @sec-verification: Adversarial Verification | Verification Matrix (`VerificationMatrix`)          | $S \cap P \cap A$ | Extreme Value Theory (EVT) tail risk bounds, hardware fault injection coverage, sim-to-real gap                                   | Rare-event tail collision, undetected hardware bit-flip, unmodeled contact compliance gap                 |
| @sec-release: Deployment Release            | Safety Case Dossier (`SafetyCaseDossier`)           | $S \cap P \cap A$ | Goal Structuring Notation (GSN) warrant validity, ASIL/SIL compliance, signed operational envelope                                | Operating outside qualified ODD, unsupported claim warrants, sign-off on unvalidated assumptions          |
| @sec-frontier: The Epistemic Frontier       | Residual-Claims Register (`ResidualClaimsRegister`) | System-wide       | Explicit uncertified premise register (such as friction floor $\mu \ge \mu_{\min}$), epistemic ceiling recognition                | Premise invalidation (such as uninspected floor oil slick), catastrophic failure beyond epistemic ceiling |

: **The S·P·A architectural contract lineage across Chapters 01 to 17**: The sixteen typed records formalize every cyber-physical boundary, linking physical plant limits to high-level policies and runtime safety cases. {#tbl-spa-lineage tbl-colwidths="[15,18,11,30,26]"}

Read in order, these records ensure that physical AI systems honor the four governing laws:

1. *First Law (Irreversibility)*: Chapters 02 to 04 derive every rate, lease, and stopping buffer directly from mechanical plant limits and fieldbus jitter.
2. *Second Law (Endogenous Data)*: Chapters 05 to 07 bind neural training and offline evaluation to closed-loop rollouts within the declared operational domain.
3. *Third Law (Proposal is Not Permission)*: Chapters 08 to 13 track one command from sensor evidence through belief, intent, and trajectory planning to the deterministic enforcer and isolated silicon.
4. *Fourth Law (Evidence Bounds Authority)*: Chapters 14 to 17 establish that a machine cannot be granted more operational authority than its empirical verification and safety cases justify.

## Physical AI Production Troubleshooting Matrix {#sec-appendix-spa-troubleshooting}

When an operational machine violates physical limits or software invariants, use @tbl-spa-troubleshooting to match observable diagnostic symptoms to the binding axis and high-leverage remedy.

| Observable symptom                                                  | Candidate boundary | Discriminating measurement                                                                                | Candidate response                                                                                                   |
|:--------------------------------------------------------------------|:-------------------|:----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Contact hunting while the arm opens the spring-latched cage door    | $A\cap S$          | Measure phase margin and force rise against the sensor-to-torque delay under the actual contact stiffness | Qualify a local impedance loop, approach-speed limit, and passive compliance for that contact                        |
| Torque or current transient at an action-chunk seam                 | $P\cap A$          | Compare encoder, phase-current, and requested acceleration traces at the measured entry state             | Admit a state-matched $C^2$ bridge and reserve a stopping suffix; the reduction in @sec-planning is profile-specific |
| Phantom obstacle stop in an aisle                                   | $S\cap P$          | Distinguish observed free, occupied, and unknown rays; inspect per-voxel evidence age                     | Clear only observed free space and retest the occupancy-to-permission conversion                                     |
| Enforcer misses its configured deadline during camera ingress       | $S\cap P\cap A$    | Correlate response-time misses with bus queue, bank switches, cache misses, and DMA ownership             | Qualify QoS bypass or a coherent local safety snapshot; remeasure under contention                                   |
| Link or workpiece yields during contact                             | $A$                | Compare measured force and displacement with the tested material and tooling limits                       | Reduce admitted speed or force and qualify a compliant load path                                                     |
| Policy update arrives after its admitted chunk horizon              | $P\cap A$          | Measure the update tail, lease expiry, and fallback transfer state                                        | Shorten the admitted action or use a stop the permission path owns; do not extend permission from a percentile alone |
| Safety microcontroller (MCU) rail droops during accelerator bursts  | $S\cap P\cap A$    | Measure rail waveform, path slack, supervisor threshold, and resulting response time                      | Characterize decoupling, current slew, or physical power isolation                                                   |
| Base drifts toward a rack face despite low offline prediction error | $A\cap S$          | Compare closed-loop yaw bias, lateral clearance, and surface-dependent braking                            | Test closed-loop rollouts and impose a feasible corridor and stop bound                                              |

: **Physical AI production troubleshooting matrix**: Each row is a hypothesis, measurement, and candidate remedy; acceptance depends on the machine's declared limits. {#tbl-spa-troubleshooting tbl-colwidths="[22,13,33,32]"}

## The S·P·A Systems Scorecard {#sec-appendix-spa-scorecard}

Before release, use @tbl-spa-scorecard to name the evidence needed for each handoff. Its checks are examples, not portable pass thresholds: the signed release case must supply the actual limits, operating envelope, confidence or hard-bound semantics, and fallback for the machine.

| Boundary                             | Example acceptance check for a declared machine                                                                                                                        | Response if the check fails                                                                          |
|:-------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Sense** — capture clock            | Bound capture-to-MCU conversion error and include it in evidence age                                                                                                   | Resynchronize or withhold motion when the bound expires                                              |
| **Sense** — ingestion                | Measure worst admitted sensor/DMA queue occupancy, drop rate, and transfer time under concurrent load                                                                  | Reserve capacity or reduce sensing load; dropped frames do not renew belief                          |
| **Plan** — chunk horizon             | Admit a successor before the commit deadline, or transfer to the resident or state-matched stop                                                                        | Use measured update tails as evidence, not as a worst-case guarantee                                 |
| **Plan** — dynamics                  | Check position, velocity, acceleration, torque, and stopping suffix against the actual joint and path limits                                                           | Reject or replan an infeasible chunk                                                                 |
| **Act** — brake and contact          | Validate achieved deceleration and force response for load, wear, surface, and temperature                                                                             | Derate speed, change tooling, or refuse the untested state                                           |
| **Act** — thermal                    | Keep measured winding and drive temperature inside device ratings under the duty cycle                                                                                 | Reduce duty or enter the validated stop/hold mode                                                    |
| **$S\cap P$** — spatial evidence     | Preserve each cell's evidence epoch and distinguish observed free, occupied, and unknown                                                                               | Refuse unknown clearance or obtain a new observation                                                 |
| **$P\cap A$** — seam                 | Check the matched entry state, derivative limits, and full stopping clearance before commit                                                                            | Use the resident or state-matched stop the permission path holds if a successor is absent or invalid |
| **$A\cap S$** — reflex               | Bound sensing-to-force response against a contact-specific harm deadline                                                                                               | Reduce approach energy or add a validated passive limit                                              |
| **$S\cap P\cap A$** — compute        | Qualify the permission path's WCET against its deadline in the cycle budget of @sec-enforcement, with acquisition, validation, write, and dispatch budgeted separately | Revoke tracking permission before the cycle overrun consumes stopping margin                         |
| **$S\cap P\cap A$** — shared silicon | Measure enforcer response under worst admitted bus, rail, and thermal contention                                                                                       | Qualify QoS/local snapshots or relocate the path if isolation cannot be shown                        |
| **$S\cap P\cap A$** — permission     | Verify model/state assumptions, feasible CBF input, clock and estimate margins, and a state-matched fallback                                                           | Refuse the proposal when a premise is missing; a QP result alone proves no path safety               |

: **The S·P·A physical AI systems scorecard**: Example release checks across the three axes and their handoffs. Each row requires a case-specific threshold and evidence. {#tbl-spa-scorecard tbl-colwidths="[19,48,33]"}
